rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bare statement that someone reads without understanding gains force when followed by a verse and a poetic illustration that makes the point vivid.
rows.anchor: أن تقول فلان يكد نفسه في قراءة الكتب ولا يفهم منها شيئا وتسكت وبين أن تتلو الآية وتنشد قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Images of leafy but fruitless trees and green bitter wood make the contrast between attractive appearance and poor substance unfold vividly.
rows.anchor: وانظر إلى المعنى في الحالة الثانية كيف يورق شجره ويثمر ويفتر ثغره ويبسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Lankak’s image makes a handsome person’s ugly conduct seem to disfigure his appearance, intensifying the rebuke through representation.
rows.anchor: إذا أخو الحسن أضحى فعله سمجا رأيت صورته من أقبح الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Tammām’s second line completes the image: slander is like fire whose heat reveals agarwood’s fragrance, exposing and enhancing a hidden virtue.
rows.anchor: وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutanabbī’s bitter-mouth simile rebukes and restrains the ignorant more powerfully than directly stating that corrupt judgment mistakes right for wrong.
rows.anchor: ومن يك ذا فم مر مريض يجد مرا به الماء الزلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison to a startled or released crow conveys swift, extended flight: fear or sudden freedom drives it farther than an unhurried bird flying by choice.
rows.anchor: نظير غرابا ولم يقل غراب يطير مثلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris compares a hawk’s beak only to the curved upper stroke of a left-handed jim; the later letters clarify that the dots and lower stroke are excluded.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يشبه المنقار بالجيم والجيم خطان الأول الذي مبدأه وهو الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The follow-up explicitly narrows the comparison to the jim’s first stroke, and the poet’s mention of thought signals the care needed for such precision.
rows.anchor: فأراك عيانا أنه عمد في التشبيه إلى الخط الأول من الجيم دون تعريقها ودون الخط الأسفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about being a thick-lipped black person implies a camel that cannot recognize the speaker’s kinship or follow his nobility.
rows.anchor: فلو كنت ضبيا عرفت قرابتي ولكن زنجيا غليظ المشافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To say something has claws embedded in it represents attachment and domination by comparing it to a lion gripping prey or a hawk clutching its catch.
rows.anchor: في التعلق بالشيء والاستيلاء عليه حالة كحاله الأسد مع فريسته والبازي مع صيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa may call himself the neglected guest and depict his own deprivation to mock al-Zibriqān and accuse him of abandoning guests to hardship.
rows.anchor: ( قروا جارك العيمان لما جفوته وقلص عن برد الشراب مشافره )

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Some interpreters say Muzarrid meant foot but substituted hoof to satisfy the rhyme.
rows.anchor: فقد قالوا إنه أراد أن يقول بساق وقدم فلما لم تطاوعه القافية وضع الحافر موضع القدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the welcoming line that follows, Muzarrid’s hoof may retain a barb: it suggests the guest’s harsh journey and forceful effort driving the camel, in keeping with the earlier description of him as disheveled.
rows.anchor: فليس بالبعيد أن يكون فيه شوب مما مضى وأن يكون الذي أفضى به إلى ذكر الحافر قصده أن يصفه بسوء الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pun is valuable through useful meaning despite its surface repetition; Abū al-Fatḥ al-Bustī’s strained examples fail, while better examples make the repeated forms serve an apt thought.
rows.anchor: حسن الإفادة مع ان الصورة صورة التكرير والإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With repeated endings, the listener first expects the old word to recur, then hears a changed word; that delayed realization creates surprise and a sense of gain.
rows.anchor: تتوهم قبل أن يرد عليك آخر الكلمة كالميم من عواصم والباء من قواضب أنها هي التي مضت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the words differ from their beginnings, as in al-Buḥturī’s example, a faint expectation of repetition remains, though it is weaker than the effect of shared endings.
rows.anchor: ( بسيوف إيماضها أوجال للأعادي ووقعها آجال )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rigid insistence on a hand behind every mention of the right hand can flatten the Shammākh phrase into the trivial statement that a grasp uses the right hand.
rows.anchor: فإن اعتبار الأصل الذي قدمت وهو أنك لا ترى اليمين حيث لا معنى لليد يقف بنا على الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khansāʾ’s image of extending a hand toward glory means much the same as receiving glory’s banner in the right hand, showing how figurative use remains connected to its source.
rows.anchor: لم تجد فرقا بين أن يمد إلى المجد يدا وبين أن يتلقى رايته باليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating figurative names as severed from their original sense leads to grave misreadings and strained interpretations of distinguished speech.
rows.anchor: هذا الضرب من الغلط كالداء الدوي حقه أن يستقصي في الكي عليه والعلاج منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 50:37, Jurjānī says a person who fails to understand is pictured as though deprived of a heart, rather than simply using heart as a synonym for intellect; he compares this to figurative loss of sight or hearing.
rows.anchor: أخذه ساذجا وقلبه غفلا وقال القلب ههنا بمعنى العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image makes darkness a routed enemy fleeing the sword it drew, giving the scene human fear and motion.
rows.anchor: فتوصل إلى ذلك بأن جعل الظلام كالعدو المنهزم الذي سل السيف في قفاه فهو يهرب مخافة أن يضرب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A similar poem depicts dawn as an ambusher and night as wary; Jurjānī says al-Khālidī lifted its first line and recast dawn as drawing swords while night flees.
rows.anchor: وقد أخذ الخالدى بيته الأول أخذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz makes the rose a conscious victor that laughs at the narcissus as its season ends; this intensifies the conventional image of a blooming rose and reverses Ibn al-Rūmī’s account of their roles.
rows.anchor: وجعل الورد كأنه يعقل ويميز فهو يشمت بالنرجس لانقضاء مدته وإبار دولته وبدو أمارات الفناء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s gray hair laughs at a man’s ill-fitting attempt to act young, unlike Daʿbal’s bare reversal; the added motive makes the simile less explicit and more vivid.
rows.anchor: جعل المشيب يضحك ضحك المتعجب من تعاطى الرجل ما لا يليق به وتكلفه الشيء ليس هو من أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who sees only outward features misses true beauty; an ornamental device should never obscure the meaning it is meant to express.
rows.anchor: إذا لم تشاهد غير حسن شياتها وأعضائها فالحسن عنك مغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Overloading speech with decorative devices can obscure or damage meaning, like weighing a bride down with jewelry; skilled writers ornament only after meaning is secure.
rows.anchor: كمن ثقل العروس بأصناف الحلى حتى ينالها من ذلك مكروه في نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ’s opening of the Book of Animals prioritizes semantic fit over matching rhyme: he avoids forced pairings such as doubt with perplexity or disagreement with fairness.
rows.anchor: فقد ترك أولا أن يوفق بين الشبهة والحيرة في الإعراب ولم ير أن يقرن الخلاف إلى الإنصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acceptable pun and assonance must be summoned by the meaning; the finest examples arise without contrivance or are sought only because they fit so well, as in al-Shāfiʿī’s answer about nabīdh.
rows.anchor: لا تجد تجنيسا مقبولا ولا سجعا حسنا حتى يكون المعنى هو الذى طلبه واستدعاه وساق نحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the lover’s line, the day of separation is black, then the heart of one who never loved is added as a witty completion because the loveless heart is imagined as still darker and callous.
rows.anchor: ولقد ذكرتك والزمان كأنه يوم النوى وفؤاد من لم يعشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common phrase night like a hypocrite’s or unbeliever’s heart has some literal grounding because a heart can be conceived as black; Ibn al-ʿAmīd’s darker than unbelief is a direct equal comparison.
rows.anchor: ليل كقلب المنافق أو الكافر إلا أن في هذا شوبا من الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjānī allows reading al-Buḥturī’s line about Sunna and innovation as truth growing more beautiful when falsehood is exposed, like stars against darkness.
rows.anchor: وإن تأولت في قوله سنن لاح بينهن ابتداع أنه أراد معنى قولهم إن سواد الظلام يزيد النجوم حسنا وبهاء كان له مذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even on that reading, the image still departs from the surface by giving abstract Sunna and innovation visible colors, so one can seem to brighten the other.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه على ذلك لا يخرج من أن يكون خارجا عن الظاهر أن يمثل المعقول في ذلك بالمحسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz daringly reverses the moon’s conventional role as the standard of beauty, describing it as spotted and albino and claiming its light is weaker than the sun’s while its heat remains.
rows.anchor: أول ما يقع في النفوس إذ أريد المبالغة في الوصف بالجمال والبلوغ فيه غاية الكمال فيقال وجه كأنه القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan’s elegy turns the horror of Ibn Baqiyya’s crucifixion into honor: height becomes distinction, onlookers become a delegation at prayer, extended hands become gifts, and wind becomes a shroud.
rows.anchor: ما صنع فيها من السحر حتى قلب جملة ما يستنكر من أحوال المصلوب إلى خلافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readerly misapprehension has degrees: sometimes resemblance becomes belief, while weaker resemblance produces only a passing impression.
rows.anchor: أن التوهم على ضر بين ضرب يستحكم حتى يبلغ ان يصير اعتقادا وضرب لا يبلغ ذلك المبلغ ولكنه شىء يجري في الخاطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Padding is condemned because it contributes nothing, but a supposedly expendable phrase that unexpectedly benefits the listener is no longer empty padding.
rows.anchor: وأما الحشو فإنما كره وذم وأنكر ورد لأنه خلا من الفائدة ولم يحل منه بعائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Metaphor is a kind of simile and representation: comparison is an analogy grasped by the intellect and heart, not by hearing alone.
rows.anchor: أما الاستعارة فهي ضرب من التشبيه ونمط من التمثيل والتشبيه قياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Antithesis is semantic opposition between ideas; it cannot arise merely from opposing word forms.
rows.anchor: وأما التطبيق فأمره أبين وكونه معنويا أجلى وأظهر فهو مقابلة الشىء بضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line is difficult because its word order fails to follow the order of thought, forcing the hearer to rearrange it and disrupting the image like badly assembled geometric parts.
rows.anchor: لم يرتب الألفاظ في الذكر على موجب ترتيب المعاني في الفكر فكد وكدر ومنع السامع أن يفهم الغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A skilled imitator may be described as a learner who follows a predecessor accurately, so a craft comes to be called that predecessor’s work.
rows.anchor: صنعة فلان وعمل فلان ووضعته في بعض موضع المتعلم الذكى والمقتدي المصيب في إقتدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Analogy across different kinds succeeds only when it finds a sound, intelligible resemblance and a genuine path of fit despite their visible differences; forced likeness produces awkwardness.
rows.anchor: أن تصيب بين المختلفين في الجنس وفي ظاهر الأمر شبها صحيحا معقولا وتجد للملائمة والتأليف السوى بينهما مذهبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using a simile marker or borrowing a word does not itself make a true comparison; the writer must show a resemblance the imagination can actually grasp.
rows.anchor: إنما تكون مشبها بالحقيقة بأن ترى الشبه وتبينه ولا يمكنك بيان ما لا يكون وتمثيل ما لا تتمثله الأوهام والظنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hidden similarities already have a rational basis; the critic earns praise by finding them through difficult thought, like discovering a pearl rather than creating its value.
rows.anchor: هناك مشابهات خفية بدق المسلك إليها فإذا تغلغل فكرك فأدركها فقد استحققت الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A composite ornament or object requires parts whose forms and proportions fit; arbitrary substitute pieces cannot produce the same design, just as no impossible resemblance can be forced.
rows.anchor: فإنما استحققت الأجرة على الغوص وإخراج الدر لا أن الدر كان بك واكتسى شرفة من جهتك
